text: Understanding Git branching is important for any version control workflow. A branch lets you work on new features without affecting the main code. Developers often create feature branches to develop and test their changes safely. When the work is finished, they merge the branch back into the main project. Before merging, teams usually open pull requests so others can review the code and discuss improvements. This process keeps the project organized and reduces mistakes. By using branches, merging, and pull requests together, teams can collaborate smoothly and keep their code stable while still moving forward quickly.
